text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Parliament on Tuesday voted in favour of a bill on the administration of social insurance authorities, under which the pension and health insurance officials will be delegated and not elected.
- President Arpad Goncz remarked in Gniezno, Poland, on Tuesday, that recent developments show that the walls are tumbling down in Europe and a common Europe is beginning to become reality.
- NATO European commander in chief Gen. George Joulwan on Tuesday that Hungary is mature enough for NATO membership, but that does not mean its armed forces do not need further development.
- A total of 471,000 people were registered unemployed at the end of May, as compared to 482,300 in April, and 18,000 less than year earlier, Labour Minister Peter Kiss said on Tuesday.

- A senior IMF official endorsed Hungary's antiinflation policy at an international seminar on inflation on Tuesday. IMF deputy managing director Stanley Fischer said the current plan to curb inflation by an annual 4 to 5 percent was realistic.
- Individuals purchased the equivalent of $26 million for travel in April, the same as a year earlier, but 29 percent less than in March, the National Bank of Hungary said on Tuesday.

- The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Water will receive 55 billion forints from the central budget for infrastructural projects this year, while the Road Fund will have an additional 16 billion for this purpose, Transport, Telecommunications and Water Minister Karoly Lotz said.
- The Free Democrats will convene the Coalition Consultative Council to discuss the agreement to be signed by the Hungarian government and the Holy See.
- The state privatisation agency APV Rt will on Wednesday evaluate bids for the sale of the aluminum oxide company Ajkai Timfoldgyar, a subsidiary of the state owned Hungalu Rt.
- The economic research company GKI Rt forecasts a 10 percent increse in investment this year, spurred by rising profits, increased borrowing and more frequent bond and share issues.
